subQuests.subQuestName: Meet up at the Masters of the Night-Wind

80180102.text: We ran into quite a big group from the Abyss Order just now. Has something happened at the front?

80180108.text: No, no, relax. THEIR front line has collapsed, not ours.

80180109.text: Phew... Feels like you could've phrased that more clearly at the start... This is good news, right? Why do you still look so serious?

subQuests.subQuestName: Wait for Dainsleif to show up

80180301.text: Hmm? Were you... waiting for me?

80180302.text: It's been a while, Dain! And yeah, after we heard what went down, we figured you'd shown up.

80180303.text: You caused quite a stir, you know. Um... this is a friend of ours from Natlan. Her name's Iansan. She insisted on coming here to thank you in person.

80180304.text: It is my honor, Mr. Dainsleif.

80180305.text: Thank you for breaking the stalemate in our war against the Abyss Order. Natlan is fortunate to share a common enemy with such a mighty warrior as yourself.

80180306.text: No need to thank me. I hunt the Abyss Order for my own reasons.

80180307.text: Please don't mind him, Iansan! He always talks like that, but he's a pretty nice guy deep down.

80180308.text: It's quite alright. Uwe{RUBY#[S]Power}zo Iansan respects those of great power. It's quite clear that he meant no offense, and I am still delighted to make his acquaintance.

80180309.text: Anyway, since you're old friends, I'll leave you to catch up for now. Take your time.

80180310.text: Sure thing. You probably have plenty of other stuff to do anyway, right? Since this war isn't exactly over. See ya later, Iansan!

80180311.text: Hey, Dain, would it have killed you to be a little more polite? She's our friend!

80180312.text: Iansan, yes? I will remember the name. But I will not invest more emotion than is necessary when dealing with the citizens of The Seven. It is a matter of principle for me.

80180315.text: Ugh, so stubborn... but whatever. So anyway, Dain, do you have any new info about the Abyss Order for us? Any idea what they're trying to achieve with this war, for example?

80180316.text: Never before have I seen the Abyss Order take action on such a large scale...

80180317.text: Taken at face value, it seems highly illogical. In a war with the Natlanese, the odds are stacked firmly against them — they surely cannot be unaware of this. Their true goal must be a deeper one...

80180318.text: We thought so too! But it sounds like you're no closer to learning what that goal is than we are.

80180319.text: I've been on the case for some time. Even captured and interrogated several Abyss Order members...

80180320.text: Yet still, I am none the wiser. I can only assume they have gone to great lengths to keep their real operations a secret.

80180321.text: I have a bad feeling about this. The Abyss Order is wasting a lot of its forces attacking Natlan, so whatever they stand to gain must hold enormous value to them.

80180322.text: What do you think we should do?

80180323.text: Since we lack actionable intelligence, for now, we might as well continue to focus on the fighting.

80180324.text: Leave them to their secret plots. If they're so willing to sacrifice manpower for it, I intend to make that sacrifice greater and more painful than they could ever have anticipated.

80180325.text: If we use this opportunity correctly, I believe we can eliminate the vast majority of the Abyss Order's forces.

80180326.text: They'll never be able to mount such a large campaign ever again. That outcome is well worth our time.

80180327.text: And the sooner we can do that, the better.

80180328.text: That's right. The ideal scenario would be to destroy them before they can reach their goal.

80180329.text: Paimon gets it: Nothing in the world can satisfy you like making mincemeat out of the Abyss Order, right?

80180331.text: Wow, okay... A rare candid response from Dain...

80180501.text: ...No, we can't give them that much time...

80180502.text: Is that... Dain and Iansan discussing strategy together? Huh, looks like they're getting along just fine.

80180503.text: Morning! What are you guys talking about?

80180504.text: Ah, you're here. I have some good news to share with you.

80180505.text: We just got word from the Scions of the Canopy. Their intelligence has reported that they've discovered the Abyss Order's headquarters in Natlan.

80180506.text: After their front lines dissolved, the bulk of their forces fell back to that area. It's also where their central command is located.

80180508.text: Cinder City, huh? That tracks... seems like their kind of place. Hey, this is great! This could be our chance to crush the Abyss Order once and for all!

80180509.text: #And with any luck, maybe we'll find your {M#sister}{F#brother} there, too!

80180510.text: Yep. Our army is almost ready, and we've sent a message to Mavuika to let her know the plan. We can't really launch an operation this big without the okay from the Archon...

80180511.text: I beg to differ. This is wasting time.

80180512.text: You have the intel you need, so act on it. Every second you delay only increases the Abyss Order's odds of survival.

80180513.text: I've already explained my reasoning, Mr. Dainsleif. I understand your concern, but an immediate strike is not on the cards for us.

80180514.text: Very well, then I will go there alone. Thank you for the intel, Iansan.

80180515.text: You're gonna go on your own!? Come on, be sensible. Just wait a tiny bit longer, and you'll have a whole army going with you...

80180516.text: It's all right. I support your decision, Mr. Dainsleif.

80180517.text: Huh!? Shouldn't you be talking sense into him?

80180518.text: I admire his courage, and I believe he is strong enough to take on the Abyss Order on his own.

80180519.text: And even if things don't go to plan, he just needs to bide his time until we arrive with reinforcements.

80180520.text: Mr. Dainsleif... I wish you the very best of luck.

80180522.text: #Uh... Looks like he's waiting for you to say something, {NICKNAME}...

80180525.text: *sigh*... For a second there, Paimon actually thought he was gonna brave it alone... and then he called his own bluff.

80180201.text: Is this the place? The Abyss Order's hideout in Natlan?

80180202.text: All these years, the Abyss Order has managed to either stay hidden or fiercely defend their position... This may be the first chance I've ever had to finally make a serious dent in their forces.

80180203.text: Which reminds me — once the fighting starts, I can't promise I'll be able to have your back at a moment's notice...

80180204.text: But if you run into any Abyss-powered mechanisms, feel free to leave them to me. I'll take care of them when I can.

80180205.text: It's been so long since we fought with Dain side-by-side. Paimon's confident we can clear this place out long before Iansan arrives!

80180206.text: #And if you get to meet your {M#sister}{F#brother} again, even better. Let's go!

80181801.text: So that's what happened... Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, must have had a hand in this.

80181802.text: There's no other way that this meeting could have taken place.

80181805.text: I knew only the ending. I've always been curious about the events that led to it.

80181806.text: #When the Cataclysm first began five hundred years ago, I, as the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} of Khaenri'ah, was preparing to do my part — to fight back with all my might...

80181807.text: But then this girl, Direidyth... she found me.

80181808.text: The irony was that even as she desperately begged me to save the world... she brought me news of you.

80181809.text: I was stunned. And I was suspicious of her claim that you were searching for me... But then, she showed me the key to your Hibernation Chamber.

80181901.text: I know you always want to change fate — we both do. But this time, I won't let you succeed.

80181902.text: I cannot miss the chance to reunite with you five hundred years in the past — no matter what.

80180801.text: (Assuming he is right, then another possibility arises:)

80180802.text: (Maybe I'm in a different time and space from Direidyth. If she's Khaenri'ahn like Dain suspects, then that means...)

80180803.text: (This revived Khaenri'ah that he speaks of might actually exist... And despite hailing from that separate time and space, Direidyth has found a way to communicate with us.)

80180804.text: Whatever may be going through your mind right now, do not trust it. I urge you not to believe his lies.

80180805.text: The notion that Khaenri'ah has been revived is preposterous. Unless I see it with my own eyes, I refuse to entertain it.

80180806.text: There is only one thing that should demand our attention in this instant... and that is silencing this man for good!

80180601.text: That should be all of them, right? So... We've destroyed the Abyss Order's headquarters in Natlan, but somehow, that didn't feel satisfying at all...

80180603.text: #Are you still thinking about what that guy said, {NICKNAME}? You look really worried.

80180606.text: I understand. You think... she might be from the revived Khaenri'ah, yes?

80180607.text: I have said my piece — I doubt Khaenri'ah could be revived so easily. But if it will give you some peace of mind, you should talk to her and test your theory.

80180608.text: I will stay here and do some post-battle cleanup. Perhaps there are some clues left to be found.

80180612.text: I thought your voice and attitude seemed familiar... My mistake. I should have made sure you were dead earlier.

80180613.text: The curse of immortality has struck you too, then, Haden.

80180614.text: Five hundred years on, and you still refuse to address me as "master"...

80180615.text: Don't forget, Dainsleif. You may be the renowned "Twilight Sword," while my arm has grown too feeble to swing a blade...

80180616.text: ...But I taught you everything you know about wielding a blade.

80180617.text: Hah. Your arrogance and malice cost you all of my respect long ago.

80180618.text: Be that as it may... Under the circumstances, I see no further reason for us to fight. The curse of immortality means neither of us has a way to completely destroy the other.

80180619.text: Speak for yourself. I intend to kill you a hundred times over.

80180622.text: *cough*... Have you... finally had enough? You weren't joking then, huh...

80180623.text: Never, in all my worst nightmares, have I experienced anything close to the pain of a hundred deaths... *cough* Surely, there's no point taking out all your hatred on me alone?

80180624.text: That was just for your actions in the Abyss Order. If I took into account what you did in Khaenri'ah... You'd soon find out how much darker your nightmares can become.

80180625.text: Alright, I believe you. Still, aren't you at least a little tired now? Why don't we sit down, perhaps chat a little?

80180627.text: What? Not a fan of reminiscing about old times? Well, I suppose you don't have many fond memories to look back on.

80180628.text: I never thought you'd side with the Abyss Order, Haden.

80180629.text: #You could have easily blamed the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} for {M#her}{F#his} betrayal.

80180630.text: #Indeed. When the Cataclysm first struck, everyone prayed for the Savior to deliver them, but {M#she}{F#he} was nowhere to be found.

80180631.text: #Yes, we knew that the great Abyssal power within {M#her}{F#him} had been divided up...

80180632.text: #Yet we still despaired at {M#her}{F#his} choice to leave us.

80180633.text: #Still, I believe that everything {M#she's}{F#he's} doing now — including {M#her}{F#his} regret over what happened — comes from a genuine place in {M#her}{F#his} heart.

80180634.text: And besides, who else can we place our faith in? We are proud Khaenri'ahns, are we not? I mean... we can hardly turn to the gods.

80180635.text: #Hmph. I suppose you have changed a lot over the past five hundred years. Otherwise, I'd have never expected you to forgive {M#her}{F#him}.

80180636.text: Had you been so generous during your time at the Knight Academy as my instructor in Black Serpent Bladework, I might not have come to loathe you so much.

80180638.text: All my good deeds were clearly in the spirit of the Academy's code of chivalry. Yet I received corporal punishment for being "restless and brash."

80180639.text: And as much as it pains me to bring up his name... Even my co-student, Surtalogi, was prosecuted for following the spirit of knighthood. He even lost limbs over it.

80180640.text: There's little point discussing it now, of course, but... All of this was your doing, wasn't it, Haden?

80180641.text: You wore a mask of benevolence as you viciously suppressed the next generation of knights, all to bolster your own position and reputation.

80180643.text: What? Too cowardly to admit it?

80180644.text: ...I'm sorry, Dainsleif. I would apologize to you for those actions, truly. But the fact is...

80180647.text: Look at me — look at what has become of me. Only by the Abyss's grace have I managed to maintain this physical form.

80180648.text: But as for the rest... Memories, spirit, emotions, personality... They have long become eroded, fragmented beyond recognition.

80180649.text: Even if mine was a past steeped in sin, or in shame I once longed to hide... I would wish to remember it.

80180650.text: Without my history, I... I fear I will become another person entirely.

80180651.text: ...I would like to apologize for any misdeeds that are mine. So please, tell me everything. Tell me about the Khaenri'ah we once called home.

80180652.text: ...No wonder your personality struck me as different. Memories are indeed a crucial part of a person's identity.

80180653.text: So. The Khaenri'ah we once called home...

80180654.text: Dainsleif slowly closes his eyes. Countless memories of Khaenri'ah flood into his mind...

80180655.text: All the sights, memories, and feelings — everything etched into the heart and mind — are gradually brought back to the forefront again, alongside a feeling of nostalgia and loss.

80180656.text: Simply recalling everything seems to take a long, long time...

80180657.text: You seem to remember much... Could you tell me more about it? About our golden age?

80180658.text: I'm not interested. I have neither the time nor the sympathy.

80180659.text: Is that so... What a pity. But this will be quite sufficient, as long as the Loom of Fate heard what I could not...

80180660.text: The Loom of Fate... What have you done? Tell me.

80180661.text: I'm afraid I owe you yet another apology, Dainsleif. You were right — I lied to you earlier. Your wits are too sharp to be fooled by me.

80180662.text: The homeland hasn't yet been revived. In fact, even the Ley Line weaving is not yet complete.

80180663.text: Think of Ley Lines as the collection of memories concerning a given place. To re-weave Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines as they were five hundred years ago, we would somehow need to retrieve almost all the memories of Khaenri'ah from that age.

80180664.text: The Loom of Fate cannot weave without an abundant supply of memories...

80180665.text: And so, we relied on everyone in the Abyss Order to provide what they could. Even though fragments are all that remain in most cases, the more we all share, the more that can be restored.

80180666.text: So, the Loom of Fate is running as we speak? And the so-called "meditation" your members have been performing... its purpose was to supply the Loom with memories, wasn't it?

80180667.text: Indeed. We, a people in exile, stranded five hundred years in the future, will weave our homeland anew, and bring the nation of our dreams back into the real world. Ah, what a glorious undertaking!

80180668.text: What a shame it had to take this long. After five hundred years, most of our memories have faded — and a world woven from broken memories shall itself be broken.

80180669.text: So that's where I'm supposed to come in? You look for assistance from your mortal enemy, who has sworn to hunt you down?

80180670.text: Precisely. For you possess a ring, left to you by your elder brother, which continuously resets your body's condition...

80180671.text: Of course, your memories are susceptible to erosion just like ours. But of all Khaenri'ahns who remain, you are sure to remember the most.

80180672.text: We had to obtain the memories in your mind, whatever the price. Even if it meant sacrificing our entire army as bait.

80180673.text: ...So this was your true goal. To lure me here, guide me into a state of meditation, and access my memories...

80180674.text: So be it. A few of my fading memories for your entire army? That strikes me as a fair trade. I appreciate your generosity.

80180675.text: You're gambling everything you have on the Loom of Fate... This could be a costly mistake for you in the long run.

80180676.text: Perhaps! But that is the gamble Our Highness has chosen to make. And thanks to you... the Loom of Fate has now finished weaving the Ley Lines. New Khaenri'ah... is complete.

80180677.text: Enough about your beloved leader. You said you would pay any price for my memories, did you not?

80180678.text: In that case... Prepare to be slain another hundred times for your deception.... I hope it was worth it.

80180701.text: Don't worry, I'll make sure I find a way to get in touch! Uh, I mean... as long as you don't mind, that is...

subQuests.subQuestName: Return to the cave to investigate
Head to the Masters of the Night-Wind and talk to Iansan

80181201.text: Our hero is back! Everyone's been waiting for you.

80181202.text: The Abyss Order made a full retreat before our forces even arrived on the scene... All thanks to your efforts, no doubt? Oh, and Mr. Dainsleif's, of course.

80181204.text: #Paimon doesn't know the details, either. {NICKNAME} just... disappeared after taking Direidyth's hand... It was like they got sucked into another world.

80181205.text: #Paimon was looking all over for {M#him}{F#her}... and then {M#he}{F#she} suddenly reappeared, right back in the same spot. But looking a lot more glum.

80181209.text: #I think I got the gist of what happened... Something to do with your {M#sister}{F#brother}? I spoke with the Lord of the Night in a dream just now, and learned quite a lot.

subQuests.subQuestName: Return to the cave you were previously in

80181301.text: Before you know it, you've fallen asleep, drowning in a myriad of thoughts.

80181302.text: You faintly sense what feels like someone clasping your hand...

80181303.text: But this time, it sends you into a deep sleep, where sweet dreams await.

80180401.text: Twilight Sword, Dainsleif... Is this really what you want?

80180402.text: It is indeed. I will take every opportunity to hunt you down to the last man.

80180403.text: #So, where's {NICKNAME}'s {M#sister}{F#brother}, then? Or is this guy supposed to be in charge here?

80180404.text: So, this is a "hunt" to you... I must say, I pity you, Dainsleif. The death you dole out so readily to others is a luxury you yourself cannot enjoy.

80180405.text: But today, that is the least of your worries... Do you realize that all your years of pursuing us are being rendered utterly meaningless, even as we speak?

80180406.text: Your riddles tire me. The overwhelming advantage is ours, at least for the moment. You know what that means for you.

80180407.text: I'd like to see what makes you believe you've already won... or that you can still turn the tide of this war.

80180408.text: #Then, allow me to be frank. As far as we are concerned... Our {M#Princess}{F#Prince} has already won by other means.

80180409.text: #And I do not merely mean this battle. No, {M#Her}{F#His} Highness has achieved something far greater...

80180410.text: ...For today, the Abyss Order's greatest wish has finally been fulfilled.

80180414.text: Our Highness quietly infiltrated the Night Kingdom to exploit that realm's past experience with Ley Line reconstruction...

80180415.text: And then used the Loom of Fate... to re-weave the Ley Lines of Khaenri'ah.

80180417.text: #Wait, does this mean the attack on the Masters of the Night-Wind was all a smokescreen to give {M#her}{F#him} some cover?

80180418.text: Oh, no... This... makes too much sense...

80180419.text: Correct. As of now, our homeland has been revived...

80180420.text: And all of my comrades that you have slain, Dainsleif... They shall forget the struggles that have beset them these past five hundred years, and begin their lives anew in a Khaenri'ah restored to life.

80180423.text: Your falsehoods are riddled with flaws. My ears tire of your tedium.

80181001.text: (What is this... Could this be... The Cataclysm?)

80181002.text: (Is this... Where Direidyth is right now? So, she really is...)

80181003.text: We're... not from the same world, are we?

80181004.text: No... I come from your future.

80181005.text: Wait, but that's great! That means the world isn't going to end.

80181006.text: In that case... Tell me, what happens to Khaenri'ah? What happens to my homeland?

80181009.text: We can only fight for our future if the future is unknown. I still believe the Savior can turn things around.

80181010.text: #I'll carry on looking for {M#her}{F#him}, even if you're not there to protect me...

80181012.text: ...I've already found my Savior — it's you. You protected me, and I believe you can protect us all... you're the one who can change everything.

80181013.text: It's just... too bad that we're not from the same time or place.

80181015.text: #Oh, one last thing, before I forget. I know how much you want to find your {M#sister}{F#brother}. Surely, {M#she}{F#he} must be desperate to find you, too?

80181016.text: So... Is there anything you can give me as a memento? Proof that we met?

80181017.text: #That way, when I do find {M#her}{F#him}, I can convince {M#her}{F#him} that you're also searching for {M#her}{F#him}.

80181021.text: (If this is her future... If this is her fate...)

80189904.text: The Abyss Order retreated when we attacked their stronghold with Iansan and Citlali. This isn't their usual style.

80189905.text: No... that could have been a tactical decision. At least, I can't see how that was directly connected to the revival of Khaenri'ah.

80189906.text: According to a guard stationed near the Masters of the Night-Wind, many members of the Abyss Order were seen idling around during the lull in the conflict, even settling down to meditate.

80189907.text: Wait... Could they have been doing that to help the Loom of Fate weave new Ley Lines? But still, that's just a theory, and it also doesn't tell me anything about whether they succeeded.

80189908.text: I couldn't see the monsters that Direidyth could see, and she couldn't see the ones I could. We could only see the monsters in each other's sight after making physical contact.

80189909.text: It's Direidyth! Great, she's still here.
